reason: Glucose is outside the cell, and the picture identifies an existing transporter that can bring it in.
expectation: Glucose will enter the cell through its transporter and begin breaking down.

effect: Glucose enters through the carrier and is broken down in the cytosol, supplying some ATP and pyruvate for mitochondria.
reaction: The picture usefully locates the first ATP-producing stage outside the mitochondria.
reason: Oxygen is shown traveling toward the mitochondria, where the glucose-derived fuel can support ATP production.
expectation: The cell will use oxygen and fuel from glucose breakdown to help remake ATP, possibly with the available ADP and phosphate.

effect: Oxygen receives electrons at the end of the mitochondrial pathway; the cell is now ready for the ATP-remaking step.
reaction: The distinction between fuel supplying energy and oxygen receiving electrons is useful.
reason: ADP and phosphate are the available ingredients for remaking ATP in the respiring cell.
expectation: The cell will use energy from aerobic respiration to join ADP and phosphate into ATP.

effect: The result shows how electron flow builds a hydrogen-ion gradient that drives ATP production, leaving ATP available for the pump.
reaction: The two-panel explanation makes the connection between respiration and ATP production clearer.
reason: The remaining goal is to use ATP to pump ions, and the available ion pump is designed for that.
expectation: The pump will use ATP to move sodium and potassium across the cell membrane.

effect: The completed pump connects ATP use to sodium and potassium movement against their concentration differences, completing the chapter’s goals.
reaction: It is satisfying to see ATP production connected back to work at the cell boundary.

mostWorthwhile.text: Remaking ATP was the most worthwhile construction: the planned two-panel picture connects electron flow, the hydrogen-ion gradient and ATP production rather than relying on the powerhouse slogan.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding glucose was relatively predictable, although the picture was useful in locating the first ATP-producing stage in the cytosol.

surprise.text: The oxygen step clearly distinguished oxygen receiving electrons and becoming part of water from fuel supplying energy.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the available ingredients and goals gave each a clear purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how similarly concrete constructions connect cell processes to tissues and organs, especially given the clear link here between ATP production and membrane transport.
